split_question: Should a landlord be barred from passing the cost of its own legal fees to a leaseholder who challenges a service charge, unless a court or tribunal says so?
angles: Make landlords carry the cost of disputes
Fix the bills themselves, not just the paperwork
poll_note: No poll used. The only published survey found (Propertymark, a trade body, 15 Jul 2026, 1,200+ leaseholders) is four months older than the news date and asks a different question, so it is not set as the poll.
facts_for_writers: From 1 April 2027 landlords need court or tribunal approval to pass on their legal costs of a service charge challenge, and leaseholders gain a right to recover their own legal expenses. [s1]

From 1 November 2027 private landlords must use standard demand forms and give accounts and annual reports; councils and housing associations follow from 1 November 2028, given an extra 12 months because of the complexity of their systems. [s1]

The government says the staggered timetable gets protections to leaseholders quickly while giving landlords time to adjust billing and accounting systems; its release gives no cost figures for landlords, councils or government. [s1]

A Propertymark survey of more than 1,200 leaseholders found 86% of those who paid a service charge saw an increase in the past 24 months, and 89% said unfair charges are difficult to challenge (a trade body's own survey, not a polling company's). [s2]
The Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill, due before Christmas 2026, would cap existing ground rents at 250 pounds and replace the forfeiture system. [s1]
